title: automation: tenant RBAC bootstrap for Private installer (Helm + Terraform)
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds automation for tenant RBAC bootstrap used by Private installer (Helm/Terraform). No user-visible API changes.
description:
Motivation: Private deployments need a deterministic, auditable RBAC bootstrap for tenant isolation during cluster provisioning and upgrades. This PR wires tenant-role and bootstrap-permission generation into the Private installer automation paths (Helm chart and Terraform module) so Fresh installs and upgrades create consistent RBAC bindings without manual steps.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces a tenant-rbac Helm subchart that renders Namespace, Role, RoleBinding, and ClusterRole templates driven by values supplied by the installer. 2) Adds a Terraform module wrapper that invokes the same templating logic (via rendered Helm chart artifacts) during automated bootstrap in air-gapped and VPC installs. 3) Adds automation scripts used by the private-installer CI to validate RBAC artifacts and simulate tenant isolation (namespace-creation + permission smoke tests). 4) Adds docs and a rollout/rollback playbook for operators.

Implementation notes: - Helm: new chart at charts/tenant-rbac, templates include parameterized rules for admin/serviceaccount separation, support for custom KMS service accounts, and optional audit annotations. Values schema validates role-scoped permissions, allowed API groups, and an allowlist for cluster-scoped bindings. - Terraform: module private/tenant_rbac wraps helm_release rendering and exposes variables that mirror the Helm values; it also emits a rendered_k8s_manifest output for downstream modules. - Installer hooks: the private-installer calls the Terraform module during initial bootstrap and during upgrades (pre-upgrade dry-run then apply) with a deterministic name prefix to prevent collision. - Security: least-privilege defaults; all elevated bindings require explicit enable flag and a linear task is required to approve for enterprise installs.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for Helm value rendering and Terraform plan validation. Added an integration test in perf-canary that runs the private-installer in a dev VPC, verifies namespace isolation, serviceaccount token scoping, and that tenant-scoped RoleBindings cannot access other namespaces. CI noted one flaky e2e run that required rerun; subsequent runs passed.

Rollout & upgrade notes: - Non-breaking: default values preserve current behavior. - During upgrades, installer runs a preflight plan to detect potential role name collisions; if collisions are detected it aborts and emits a remediation plan in the installer log. - Rollback: the Terraform module supports a "revert_to_previous" input which re-applies the last known good rendered manifest (operator must provide the last applied output). Playbook in docs/RBAC_BOOTSTRAP_ROLLBACK.md included.

Security considerations: audit annotations are added to all ClusterRoleBindings created by automation. KMS/HSM service accounts are not created by this module by default; there is an opt-in path for managed-service accounts. All changes are covered by the existing RBAC policy-review workflow (Linear ENG-4237).

Notes for reviewers: focus on the Helm value schema (charts/tenant-rbac/values.schema.json), Terraform module interface (modules/tenant_rbac/README.md), and the installer hook idempotency guarantees. The PR intentionally separates rendering from apply so air-gapped installs can review manifests before applying.

Checklist: - [x] Helm chart and schema added - [x] Terraform module wrapper added - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Docs and rollback playbook - [x] Security review request opened

Related: ENG-4237, ENG-4299, SUP-1124
